# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

No inventor passage separates the pin from the force-limiting spring stack, and the disclosure ties the pin's motion to stack compression, so the drawing as written would have depicted a pin that cannot perform its disclosed function under claims 4, 12 and 15. The words are deleted, not replaced with an invented drive linkage, because the source does not say how the pin is driven. (2) Major: FIG. 2's frame annulus is now divided by radial breaks at the left and right in line with the cam-ring band divisions, so the principal interior view no longer reads as a one-piece frame carrying a segmented ring, contrary to FIG. 1 and to the split-frame disclosure. (3) Minor: claim 16 now introduces "a respective carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward" instead of the bare plural "carriage springs", curing the antecedent-basis defect in method claim 14's chain using wording already present in the detailed description. No application text was widened; both figure fixes were made in figures/ only. Verified by hand: 28 numerals, one part each, all used in the detailed description, every sheet numeral in the table, the four sheets covering all 28, no sheet above eight numerals, Brief Description in step with each brief, and no placeholder, drafting note or em dash in draft/ or figures/. Two limits stated plainly rather than papered over: no drawing sheet was actually missing (all four disclosed views already exist, so nothing was generated), and I did not and cannot run the render, OCR, leader-endpoint or independent-review gates, since those belong to the image pipeline and reviewer and I am barred from creating image files; readiness should be published from that run, not from this turn. Per the drafting brief, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and the art available to this application may be incomplete.
reasoning: The FIG. 4 finding was correct and substantive. A brief that says a functional rod is 'clear of' the spring stack and terminates inside the housing is a contact statement, not a rendering hint, and the only source passage on the pin runs the other way: the pin moves relative to a fixed edge when the stack enters a predetermined compression range. I deleted the negative relationship and the termination clause and stopped there. Inventing a visible linkage between rod and stack would have been the worse error, since the disclosure is silent on how the pin is driven, so the sheet now shows the rod rising through the top wall with its upper end visible and says nothing about what it touches.

The FIG. 2 finding was also correct: the split frame is the whole premise of the invention, and the interior view had the cam-ring band divided while the frame around it was continuous. Restoring the radial breaks adds no structure that is not already in FIG. 1 and in the inventor's first sentence. I described the halves generically as an upper half and a lower half rather than by their canonical part names, because 12 and 14 are not listed on that sheet and a canonical name there would create a stale-numeral defect.

Claim 16 was a pure form defect, so I fixed it in form only. Method claim 14 recites jaw carriages but never a spring, so 'under carriage springs' had nothing to refer back to. Introducing 'a respective carriage spring biasing each jaw carriage outward' inside claim 16 gives the term its own antecedent without narrowing the claim, and it reuses the exact words of the detailed description ('A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward') so the support is literal.

I deliberately left claim 1 alone. Its limitations, the segmented cam ring whose segments are coupled into a working ring by the act of closing the frame plus the force-limiting spring stack in the drive path between handle and wedge, are the disclosed essential relationship, and nothing in the review challenged them. A narrowing or rewording here would have been scope given away for no gate.

I edited only the two figure briefs and one claim. The request's broader words about completing the package did not license reworking the background, summary or description, all of which I checked and found consistent, so touching them would only have destroyed prior wording and made the change log useless.
